title: Emit audit log events for rollback policy changes and automated rollback actions
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Problem
- Auto-rollback will change customer traffic split / effective model version without a human clicking a button. For compliance (SOC2, ISO27001 change tracking) and for customer trust, we must produce attributable, exportable audit events.
- We also need audit coverage for rollback policy configuration changes (who changed threshold/window/cooldown/etc) because those changes materially impact production behavior.

Scope
1) Emit audit events for:
   A. Rollback policy changes (create/update/delete/enable/disable)
   B. Auto-rollback trigger decision ("verdict" transitions) + why
   C. Rollback executor actions (traffic split revert, version pin/fallback actions)
2) Ensure events are searchable in Redwood Audit Log UI and exportable to customer SIEM (existing pipeline).
3) Define and implement event schema (stable; versioned) and update compliance checklist.

Non-goals
- No new audit storage backend.
- No console UX work beyond making sure fields are present for the Console API to render.

Event types (proposed)
1) rollout.rollback_policy.updated
- Emitted on create/update/delete, and on enable/disable.
- Actor: user/service

2) rollout.auto_rollback.verdict_changed
- Emitted when verdict transitions: healthy -> breached, breached -> rollback_pending, rollback_pending -> rolled_back, or to suppressed/unknown.
- This is the "decision" record; should include monitor identity and the policy evaluation context.

3) rollout.auto_rollback.executed
- Emitted when executor applies rollback (traffic split revert to stable, etc).
- Must include idempotency key and resulting state.

4) rollout.auto_rollback.execution_failed
- Emitted when executor attempted action but failed (routing API error, conflict, validation).

5) rollout.auto_rollback.suppressed
- Emitted when breach detected but suppressed due to guardrails (min traffic not met, warm-up window, cooldown active, stale monitor, global rate limit, manual pause).

Schema requirements (must-have fields)
Applies to all event types unless noted.
- event_type: string (see above)
- event_version: integer (start at 1)
- occurred_at: RFC3339 timestamp
- request_id / trace_id: propagate from control plane request context where available
- actor_type: user | service
- actor_id: user id or service principal (e.g., rollout-controller)
- actor_display: best-effort human readable (email for user, service name for service)
- tenant_id: Redwood tenant/org identifier
- environment: hosted | dedicated | private (if known)
- region: e.g., us-east-1
- rollout_id: rollout identifier
- route_id / route_name: logical API route (or deployment route)
- model: model name (e.g., llama-3.1-70b)
- from_version / to_version: model serving versions involved (for policy update: old/new policy version; for rollback executed: candidate->stable)
- customer_tier: hosted | dedicated | enterprise (if present in monitor identity)

Additional fields by event
A) rollout.rollback_policy.updated
- change_type: created | updated | deleted | enabled | disabled
- policy_id
- policy_scope: route/model/region/tier
- diff_summary: short string (no secrets) e.g., "p95_latency_ms threshold 900->750; cooldown 10m->20m"
- policy_snapshot: JSON string (sanitized) OR pointer (preferred) to config version hash

B) rollout.auto_rollback.verdict_changed
- previous_verdict / new_verdict: healthy | breached | rollback_pending | rolled_back | suppressed | unknown
- reason: enum string (latency_slo_breach | error_slo_breach | both | monitor_unavailable | min_traffic_not_met | cooldown_active | warmup_window | baseline_not_worse | rate_limited)
- monitor_identity: canonical string per ADR-0147 (include labels route/model/region/tier + slo_type)
- evaluation_window: e.g., "5m" / "10m"; include multi-window if used
- observed_values: string (sanitized) e.g., "p95=842ms threshold=750ms; 5xx_rate=1.8% threshold=1.0%"
- baseline_values: optional string when "must-be-worse-than-baseline" enabled

C) rollout.auto_rollback.executed
- action: revert_traffic_split | revert_model_version | disable_rollout | pin_previous
- traffic_before / traffic_after: string (e.g., "canary=25% stable=75%" -> "canary=0% stable=100%")
- idempotency_key
- executor_result: success

D) rollout.auto_rollback.execution_failed
- action
- idempotency_key
- error_class: validation | conflict | dependency_unavailable | unknown
- error_message: truncated and scrubbed

Data handling / compliance notes
- Do not log prompts, completions, request bodies, or customer headers.
- Do not log raw metric series. Only log aggregated numbers needed to justify decision.
- Redact any free-form strings coming from monitors/alerts (enforce allowlist formatting).
- Ensure events include enough context for customer audit and for oncall triage.

Implementation plan
- Add audit emitter calls at three boundaries:
  1) Policy write path (create/update/enable/disable) in control plane config service.
  2) Evaluator verdict transition (state machine) in rollout-controller.
  3) Executor action completion/failure in rollout-controller.
- Use existing audit logging client + async publish (do not block rollback actions on audit pipeline).
- Add unit tests for: schema validation, redaction, and event emission on each transition.
- Add integration coverage in synthetic SLO breach test harness: verify audit events are produced for (a) breach -> rollback executed, and (b) breach suppressed.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] All event types above emitted with required fields.
- [x] Events are visible in internal Audit Log search within 5 minutes (existing ingestion SLO).
- [x] Events export correctly via SIEM export path (spot-check with Kevin Osei).
- [x] No secrets/PII/payloads appear in emitted events (redaction tests).
- [x] Compliance review checklist completed + sign-off recorded.

Compliance review checklist (to be completed before enabling default-on)
- Field review: all fields are in allowlist; no user payloads.
- Redaction review: error messages truncated; monitor names normalized; labels strictly formatted.
- Access control: audit log query respects tenant isolation.
- Retention: matches customer plan (no new retention class required).
- Export: event types mapped for SIEM export.
- Change management: schema versioned and documented.

Open questions
- Do we need separate event types for manual rollback vs automated rollback, or do we reuse executor events with actor_type=user vs service?
  -> Proposal: reuse same event types; distinguish via actor_type/actor_id.
- For Private/on-prem: do we always have tenant_id/region? If missing, enforce "unknown" but still emit.

Notes / coordination
- Security/Compliance reviewers: Naomi Feldman, Marcus Lin
- SRE input requested: Rafael Mendes (oncall needs: include links/ids to correlate with incident-bot messages)
comments: 2025-01-23 (Jordan Lee): Creating as P0 because auto-rollback without auditability will be blocked for enterprise tenants. Please keep schema tight; no free-form payloads.
2025-01-24 (Naomi Feldman): Add explicit event for suppression decisions. Auditors will ask why an automated control *did not* act. Also ensure actor_type=service for evaluator/executor.

2025-01-28 (Michael Nguyen): Drafted schema as per Confluence audit spec. Implementing as versioned structs in control-plane + rollout-controller emitter wrappers. Will default unknown fields to "unknown" instead of dropping events.
2025-02-02 (Marcus Lin): Security review: ensure error_message is scrubbed and truncated; prohibit logging query strings that may include customer identifiers. +1 on allowlisted reason enums only.
2025-02-06 (Rafael Mendes): Oncall ask: include rollout_id + route_name + region + monitor_identity in every verdict/executed event. We correlate these in incident-bot + dashboards.

2025-02-10 (Michael Nguyen): Landed PR-18488. Added tests for redaction + schema validation. Integration test harness updated to assert at least 3 events on breach->rollback path (verdict_changed, executed, policy unchanged).

2025-02-12 (Naomi Feldman): Compliance sign-off granted for event schema v1. Please document schema in Confluence (same page) and note that future field additions require version bump if semantics change.
